incomplete: This sample is not complete. I ran out of search calls before finishing the following. (1) Philosophical Review: 134(1) has only one research article, so rule 5 sends the other two picks to 134(2) (April 2025). I could not retrieve that table of contents and did not guess. 'Fictional Reality' (Blumberg & Holguín, doi 10.1215/00318108-11676103, pp. 149–201) is in 134(2), but I could not confirm its position, so it is not listed. (2) Journal of Philosophy: the first 2025 issue is the double issue 122(1/2), which contains only the Dewey Lectures. I counted the lectures as research articles because rule 3 does not exclude them. Lecture II's title was checked against the PDC special-issues page, but I did not find its DOI. I did not find Lecture III's title, so I left it out. Pick two more articles from the next issue, vol. 122 no. 3, if you do not want the lectures. (3) DOIs and open-access copies are unverified (null) for Bird, Metz, Hornett and Himelright & Murgueitio Ramírez. They are also unverified for the Mind articles except Goldstein & Hawthorne's preprint. The Mind DOIs listed come from the issue table of contents. (4) Judgment call: the Goldstein & Hawthorne paper argues from what speakers say and refrain from saying, and PhilPapers lists 'Assertion' among its keywords. I treated its subject as the KK principle and included it. If you read rule 4 more strictly, skip it and take the next Mind article, 'Intentions and Inquiry' (Daniel C. Friedman, doi 10.1093/mind/fzae056). (5) Dogramaci & Schoenfield's Boltzmann-brain paper is a Bayesian argument about evidence and skepticism. I did not treat it as a paper about credence or confidence.
